output.name: Sokul

anatomy.part: breast, the middle of the body
right wing elbow, the bright shoulder joint

output.myth: When Aun cut the string, the sky went off like a sail torn from its mast, and Tavo laughed so hard the cliffs rang. A gull named Sokul was working the north ledges that morning with a cod in its beak. It saw the sky leaving and went after it, higher than any gull had flown. Tavo took the bird by one wingtip and bent it back, and Sokul had to stoop to come home, and it came home with the fish still in its beak. Hesk counted the wing. Ennu says the bend is why the gulls ride the wind so close to the cliffs, always testing it. The Gulls, who carry word between Vel and the islands, say Sokul is still aloft, and that when its bent wing points at the house, someone will fly back. Mend your own tears with sinew. Watch the gull's wing before you fly.
output.verse:
One bent wing bends back
the gull stoops low to the cliff
Hesk counts each wing home
